children: oilseed refining plant in Dnipro and another facility in Mkyolaiv, Ukraine, have been damaged by Russian drone strikes as Moscow targets Ukraine’s food industry.

One person was killed and 10 were injured by the Dnipro strike, the third time the facility has been struck this year amid the ongoing conflict between Ukraine and Russia. The Dnipro plant is responsible for roughly 40% of Ukraine’s sunflower processing capacity.

Last week, Ukraine intelligence warned that Moscow was preparing strikes on the country’s vegetable oil industry, including foreign-owned facilities. Sunflower is one of Ukraine’s key food exports and accounts for approximately 9% to 10% of total Ukrainian exports and 3.2% of pre-war GDP.

Bunge’s sunflower processing business is part of its Softseed Processing and Refining segment. While processing capacity is spread across the globe, Europe represents 53% of Bunge’s softseed processing capacity, with the Dnipro plant responsible for the export of 1,600 tons of oilseeds per day.
with analysts, Bunge’s CEO Gregory Heckman warned that the war in Ukraine is having a “complex and difficult” impact on production.

“With Russia and Ukraine together being about 25% of global exports on wheat, that slowed down as the seaborne has been forced to go overland. It’s less competitive, less volume getting out, and as that’s constrained, that’s pulling on a lot of other origins,” Heckman said during the call.
shares are down more than 2% on Monday.

title: Bunge Global's Ukraine sunflower processing plants hit by drones
